The two minor findings (R1 exotic-regime admission gap, R2 non-f32/f64 dtype swallow inherited from C6-20) are unreachable from every regime and dtype the product or its tests produce, do not affect values, and have one-line closures; the record's 'values AND warnings on the whole admitted domain' wording should be corrected either way.

findings.claim: patch_radiation.py:1221-1228 admits every regime with divide/invalid != 'raise', but replicates the removed log warnings only when divide == 'warn'. For the redirected channels divide='call'/'print'/'log' (admitted, not silenced) the original body's floating-point error handling is swallowed.
findings.evidence: Probe (reviewer-written, .venv python): np.seterr(divide='call') with a seterrcall hook and svfS==1 in-domain: twin divide-hook hits = 0, serial body hits = 1 (MISMATCH); outputs still bitwise. Pre-S10-23 behavior: the C6-20 guard declined every non-default regime, so the body ran and the hook fired - this is a user-observable regression in an admitted regime. Root cause: the admission rule excludes only 'raise' while the twin docstring justifies admission only for 'silenced' channels ('with divide='ignore' the replicated log cannot warn') - 'call'/'print'/'log' redirect rather than silence, so code admits more than its stated justification. Same gap applies to invalid='call'/'print'/'log' in principle, but f32/f64 in-domain inputs have no invalid emitters (bounds-verified), so it is only reachable through the float16 surface of R2. Not production-reachable: grep over src/ and tests/ shows zero uses of divide/invalid 'call'/'print'/'log' or seterrcall; the pipeline leaks divide/invalid='ignore' (engine.py:333, verified).
findings.recommended_closure: Either (a) tighten the rule to divide/invalid in {'warn','ignore'} (one-line change + one regime-matrix case), or (b) keep the rule and correct residual_parity.json admission_rule + the twin docstring to state that redirected channels are admitted without replication. Option (a) preferred: it restores the pre-S10-23 observable contract for those regimes and makes the 'values AND warnings on the whole admitted domain' claim true.

findings.claim: _anisotropic_domain does not constrain dtype, so float16 in-domain inputs (svf in [0,1], |Ta| <= 1000, ...) are admitted, and the removed float16 chains overflow/invalid-warn ((Ta+273.15)**4 in float16 -> inf at Ta>=~295) under over='warn' - warnings the twin never computes. The record's 'bit-level parity on the whole admitted domain (values AND warnings)' is overbroad for non-f32/f64 dtypes.
findings.evidence: Probe (reviewer-written): float16 svf/Ta in-domain case -> twin route = primary (admitted), reference body emits 9-11 warnings ('overflow encountered in power', 'invalid value encountered in multiply'), twin emits 0; values bitwise. PRE-EXISTING, not a regression: the shipped C6-20 path has the identical property - probe shows _guard_anisotropic.ok = True on the same case (default regime) and lside_veg_v2022a_demanded(PIPELINE_CYLINDER_ANISOTROPIC) returns via the fast path with 0 warnings where the body emits 9. For f32/f64 the claim holds: static bound analysis (largest removed-chain intermediate ~(1273.15)^4 ~= 2.6e12 and the Lvikt polynomial on svfvegbu <= 101 gives ~1e14, both far below float32 max; exp argument <= 0 so exp cannot overflow; tan argument |x| <= ~3140 stays finite) plus an executed probe at the extreme in-domain bounds (azimuth/t/altitude +/-1e6, Ta/Tw/F_sh/CI +/-1000, SBC/ewall/esky +/-100, svf 0/1 mixes, veg/aveg 100, Lup/Ldown at f32 max) produced zero over/invalid warnings from the body.
findings.recommended_closure: Either dtype-gate the svf/veg/aveg/scalar bounds checks to float32/float64 (the characterized dtypes) or correct the claim wording in residual_parity.json/s10_23_lside_dispatch_twin.md to 'values bitwise on the whole admitted domain; warning parity for the characterized float32/float64 domain'. The twin inherits the swallow from shipped C6-20, so either closure is a documentation/qualification tightening, not a bug fix.

exactness_derivation.code_reading: engine.py:1340-1479 read in full: the four anisotropic_longwave==1 branches assign Lground = _operate(np.multiply, LupX, 0.5) and return (Least, Lsouth, Lwest, Lnorth) - no other term reaches the returned fields on that branch; _operands/_operate use the identical call shape in _demanded_anisotropic_result; the body converts only azimuth/altitude/ewall/t/anisotropic_longwave through _array(copy=True), so Lup* reach the multiply unconverted in both implementations; F_sh is rebound, never mutated; both implementations return fresh ufunc outputs (no aliasing).
exactness_derivation.order_and_replication: log_dirs indexing 0..3 runs over (svfE, svfS, svfW, svfN) in _anisotropic_domain; the twin's replicate call passes (values['svfE'], values['svfS'], values['svfW'], values['svfN']) - same E,S,W,N order as the body's svfalfaE/S/W/N and the return order. Replication re-executes subtract+log once per affected direction, matching the body's single log per direction (probe: 2+2 warnings in a dispatch+reference pair with two affected directions).
exactness_derivation.adversarial_probes: 20+ cases, all bitwise + 4-tuple contract + no aliasing + no input mutation: baseline f32 profile; extreme in-domain bounds (day altitude=1e6 and night altitude=-1e6, azimuth/t +/-1e6, Ta/Tw/F_sh/CI +/-1000, SBC/ewall/esky +/-100, svf 0.0/1.0/0.5 mixes, veg/aveg 100/0, Lup/Ldown at float32 max); strided base[::2,::2] views; read-only arrays; mixed f32/f64 svf/F_sh/Ldown/Lup; NaN Lup admitted; NaN svf decline; empty (0,0) arrays decline; aniso in {True, np.float32(1), 0-d int array, 1.0}; leaked regime with svf==1 (both silent); promoted-warning (simplefilter('error')) -> RuntimeWarning raised from the original site; divide='call' (finding R1); float16 in-domain (finding R2).
exactness_derivation.warning_regime_analysis: (i) YES - the shipped C6-20 demanded fast path already has the same swallow property under the default regime (over='warn'): it computes only the four multiplies and never runs the removed chains; the twin is consistent with that shipped precedent. (ii) For float32/float64, YES - the bounds exclude every over-emitter (largest intermediates ~2.6e12 and ~1e14 vs float32 max 3.4e38; exp argument <= 0; tan argument <= ~3140), confirmed by a probe at the extremes showing zero over/invalid warnings from the body; for float16, NO (finding R2). (iii) No production-reachable in-domain f32/f64 case found where the body prints an over-warning the twin suppresses; the only swallow surfaces found are the exotic redirected divide channels (R1) and non-f32/f64 dtypes (R2), neither producible by any code in this repository (grep: no 'call'/'print'/'log' errstates, no seterrcall; production rasters are float32).
